completeness-consistency: Not ready for assembly, but fixable in one revision pass. The engineering core is coherent: sections 04, 05 and 08 implement recommended.md faithfully, the gate set is machine-checkable, and the three reviewer notes that do depart (Manifest/Range Index, server-computed ICC, Rust-vs-TS exit) are the right calls. As a complete project plan it fails on completeness and consistency. Completeness: the regulatory/QMS/free-distribution/funding section that the programme context makes mandatory does not exist; all twelve sections defer to it, and they do so on the false premise that research note 11-gap-8 is missing (it exists and reverses note 09 on the product code, verified today as QKQ). Consistency: the sections disagree on the calendar (three M0 dates, Stage 0 of 2, 3 or 6 weeks, a TSP data freeze dated after the January meeting, devices bought after the gates that need them), on the release timing of roughly a dozen pillar features, and on the repository conventions agents will encode in week 1 (two execution-loop designs, three ADR registers with contradictory licence wording, two requirement-ID namespaces, two gate-file formats, two provenance paths, two repo layouts). Three architectural contradictions must be settled before the Manifest and Dx-pathway freezes because they change the latency arithmetic or the pathway definition: 512-px grid versus 240/256-px passthrough frames, 'server-baked ICC' versus byte passthrough, and 'no request-time transcoding, ever' versus the moving tier. Most fixes are propagation of a decision one section has already made correctly (04 on the Manifest, 05 on colour, 10 on the Stage-0 calendar, 11 on TSP facts, 07 as schedule owner), plus writing section 13 from gap-8.
perf-realism: The plan is unusually disciplined about measurement (REF-relative gates, quality record, golden replay, Stage-0-before-claims) and its desktop/LAN promise is credible. Its floor-device promise is not yet credible as written: on W-4G and W-iPad the arithmetic does not close in several independent places, and the sections contradict each other on the inputs. Specifically: (1) the per-frame upload budget (2–4 MiB) cannot coexist with the 3 ms time box and the G5 ceiling of 2 ms/tile, so the cold-fill rows and the M2 "≤10 frames" gate are 2× optimistic; (2) the byte model (80 KB/tile, 2–5 MB Base Bundle) is contradicted by the project's own measured pyramid (103–123 KB at coarse levels, 9.5 MB Base Bundle; 4:4:4 adds 24 %), which stretches every 4G/broadband transfer term 1.5–1.9×; (3) the in-flight and prefetch constants (24 slots, 0.5·bw·0.5 s) are 5–14× the bandwidth-delay product on 4G and broadband, so tier-0 requests queue ~250 ms behind the viewer's own prefetch, while the same constants starve the prefetch that CHS ≥ 85 % depends on; (4) the W-4G gate set is self-inconsistent (TTS p95 ≤ 700 ms cannot hold with 15 % cold settles whose p50 is 650 ms); (5) the 128 MiB L0 budget is undercounted (ancestor chain omitted, average not worst-case tile counts) and the DPR cap is keyed to the network rather than to the memory it protects; (6) the 16-bit multichannel path has no residency or bandwidth model at all yet is gated "on the same devices"; and (7) a documented Mali/TBDR jank source — writing into a texture array still referenced by in-flight draws, which the driver resolves by ghost-copying the whole 64 MiB array or stalling — is absent from the 37-cause table and from G12's measurement protocol. None of these is an architecture exit; all are fixable in a numbers pass before Stage 0's measurement protocol is frozen. Recommendation: hold the plan at "conditionally approved": fix the seven high items (re-derive §2/§5/§9/§13 of section 05 from the measured pyramid and a BDP-based scheduler, add the in-use-texture row and the multichannel table, reconcile the W-4G gates), propagate the corrected constants to sections 01/02/04/08/RA, and make Stage 0 measure G12 into an in-use array. The medium items should be closed by M1; the low items are editorial reconciliation.
feasibility-delivery: NOT READY TO EXECUTE AS WRITTEN; FIXABLE IN ONE REVISION PASS. The engineering content (architecture, gates, measurement stack, agent loop) is unusually strong and internally consistent on the technical axis. The delivery axis is not: the plan is scheduled for a funded 5.5→16 FTE reference team whose graphics seniors are "hired before week 0" (Monday 2026-10-26, two days away) while the actual programme is an unfunded resident plus AI agents with no costed compute budget; M0 carries four different dates (Nov 20 / Nov 30 / Dec 5 / "≈month 2") across §07/§09/§10/§08; the TSP milestone in §07 is built on an unverified "early February" meeting date when the verified meeting (22–24 Jan 2027) ends five days BEFORE the M1 "data freeze"; the MVP carries 32 Must requirements plus desktop, fluorescence, two canonical stores and six education features, so it is not minimal and dilutes the one thing that matters (M2: goal 1 on real floor devices); and research note gap-8 (which landed after the sections were written) contradicts the plan on IEC 62304 class (C vs B), on RUO/Dx/Edu as separate builds vs a mode flag, on product code (QKQ vs PSY) and on when the Pre-Sub, QMS and scanner/display partner work must start. Two items are not in any section at all and sit on the UT critical path: Regents' Rule 90101/OTC approval before an Apache-2.0 release by a UT employee, and TX-RAMP for any cloud-hosted service a UT institution uses (education pilot, clinical pilot). Fix the date anchors, split the plan into a funded and an owner-plus-agents scenario with an explicit funding gate, shrink the MVP to the M2 proof, pull the regulatory and IP prerequisites (OTC, Pre-Sub, Class C segregation, lightweight QMS) into 2027, and propagate the gap-8 corrections; then the plan is executable and the January 2027 TSP presentation (M0 + Tier-2 nightly trend, not M1) is credible.
user-integrator: The plan is unusually strong on what it set out to optimise — the instant-zoom engine, the measurement discipline and the integration surfaces are specified to a level an agent can implement against — but, read as a sign-out pathologist, a fluorescence researcher, an ML engineer, a hospital integrator and an iPad teacher would read it, it bakes in several dead-ends that must be fixed before assembly. Eight are high: (1) the clinical pillar runs diagnostic work (frozen-section preliminaries, sign-out write-back) under an RUO label that gap-8 F3 says cannot carry LIS integration or clinical claims; (2) the 512-px grid contradicts the byte-for-byte passthrough promise for SVS (240/256-px tiles), so the vendor-hash identity CI assertion and the research patch-export claim are false for the largest public corpus and the contradiction is frozen into the Manifest schema; (3) the research pillar's headline M5 fluorescence gate is infeasible because the 16-bit zstd-only canonical implies ~30 MB per viewport fill with no 8-bit/lossy delivery tier anywhere in the design; (4) wrong-slide/wrong-patient display is missing from every hazard list and no requirement shows the label image or binds launch context to Manifest; (5) Dx mode's 'refuses unvalidated displays' cannot be enforced in a browser, where the plan allows it; (6) the Dx colour step is defined three incompatible ways across 02/05/08/recommended; (7) gap-8 now exists and contradicts the plan on product code (QKQ not PSY), Pre-Sub timing, UT indemnification and qualification criteria; (8) the TSP presentation plan in 07 is built on an unverified February date — the verified 22–24 January meeting precedes M1. The medium issues are mostly cross-section drift (three M0 dates, HL7/CAP/LTI releases differing by section, ADR-0007 seeding the superseded 'commercial' wording, Manifest vs Range Index, Base Bundle bytes 2–4× under the plan's own measurement, 4K viewport never budgeted) that an agent pipeline will faithfully propagate, plus concrete workflow gaps (iframe-confined viewer vs diagnostic display, view-while-scanning infeasible for TIFF-family scanners, LTI cookie failure on Safari iPad, no local tiler for the model-development loop, no brightfield image adjustment). None of these requires an architecture change; all require edits to requirements, gates, labelling and a second amendment to recommended.md so the single source of truth stops being overridden in reviewer notes. Verdict: not ready for assembly or for seeding the repository ADRs until the eight high issues are resolved; with them fixed, the plan serves all three pillars credibly.
feasibility-delivery:13-regulatory-pathw: Revise before assembly; do not reject. Section 13 is the strongest regulatory treatment in the plan and its core decisions are sound and well-sourced: QKQ Traditional 510(k) with a viewer predicate and a PCCP from the first filing, a narrowly frozen Class C pixel pathway behind an architectural boundary, file regardless of the unresolved 'free = commercial distribution' question, Apache-2.0 code with a signed cleared build, a hybrid UT-institution/501(c)(3) holder, and a cost-to-clearance of $1.5–3 M that is credible (people-dominated, fees $0–45 k). Its delivery plan is not yet executable. It names the true critical path (QMS, evidence, scanner partner, institutional sponsor) and then schedules those items last while declaring 'nothing there moves', contradicting fixes already demanded by issues 53 and 54; it files the Pre-Sub before the entity decision its fifth question depends on and never schedules the institutional commitment to be a manufacturer; it starts the $150–400 k reader study before IRB approval and the HF summative before any freeze, and lets the study finish after the submission it is supposed to insure; it checks post-market funding only after obligations attach and leans on consortium dues from members who will not exist until years after FREE-1; it leaves the steward 501(c)(3) unformed and the two-entity regulatory roles unassigned; and it omits the in-house clinical build that issue 64 requires, repeating the 'RUO-labelled' diagnostic-use contradiction. The Dx 1.0 MVP is also not minimal (two renderers, all browsers, three topologies implied) and the steady-state cost borrows a period-total 20–30 PM as a per-year figure. All of this is re-sequencing, gating and quantification rather than new research: pull QMS SOPs and vendor/lab commitments into v0.x–v0.9, add a Dx RC freeze (≈W96), make the reader study conditional on Pre-Sub feedback, gate DX-0 on funded post-market duties and a signed institutional sponsor, scope Dx 1.0 to one platform/topology/two scanners/two displays, and express every regulatory gate as a repository artefact so agents can be held to it.
completeness-consistency:13-regulatory-p: Section 13 is the strongest-sourced section in the plan and closes most of what issues #0, #12, #67 and #70 asked for: product code QKQ, a predicate table, a Pre-Sub question set, a PCCP structure, a manufacturer decision matrix with Texas-law constraints, a costed reader study, qualification criteria, an onboarding pipeline, post-market duties and a funding table, all with evidence tags. It is not yet ready for assembly, for five reasons that are each fixable in one revision pass. (1) It decides three named products but leaves undefined the fourth artefact its own roadmap uses for CLIN-1 and CAP-1 (the pre-clearance in-house clinical build), which is the exact RUO-used-clinically problem issue #64 raised. (2) Its IEC 62304 boundary classes the same crates C in Dx mode and B in Nav mode and leaves the scheduler/cache that cause HAZ-1 at Class B; that is not a valid §4.3 segregation and cannot be enforced by the crate-layering test the plan relies on, and it underwrites the documentation and RX-5 estimates. (3) It freezes the Dx build only at submission while requiring bench, HF summative and reader-study evidence on the frozen build, with the reader study ending after DX-1 and IRB approval scheduled after the study starts. (4) It keeps 07's schedule ('nothing there moves') where issues #52–#54 demanded compression (Pre-Sub H1 2027, entity decision at M1, OTC approval in Sprint 1, CAP-1 and 510(k) not serialised) and keeps browsers as a Dx surface against issue #68. (5) It introduces a dozen product mechanisms (UDI/About screen, config-hash gate, attestation and banner, complaint intake, identity echo, forced updates versus site revalidation) with no REQ IDs and never writes the FR-R7/FR-R8 text it says it fills, while its cost figures mis-cite 07 §9 and disagree between §5.3/§5.4/§7/Decision 10. Secondary items: AI-overlay display in Dx mode is asserted covered by the AI vendor's clearance against 09 OQ-18; OQ-17 and OQ-02 are missing from the Pre-Sub list; QMS software validation/Part 11 and the agent-toolchain 'qualification' position are undefined; Texas public-funds doctrine and TX-RAMP are absent from §5/§6; and the propagation list to the other twelve sections names only PSY→QKQ. Fix the five primary items and publish an explicit propagation table, and the section can anchor the regulatory programme.
